title: Brown's scripted claim to have started jazz in Chicago in 1915
summary: Brown reads a script claiming he started jazz in Chicago in 1915, complains others took the credit, and reads signatures and a postscript naming his bandmates.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: There's a big ballyhoo today. Would you like to meet the man that started jazz? He's right here in your city standing fast. You shouldn't believe a word of what you've already heard. They're busy telling lies of what they've heard. Tom Brown started jazz in Chicago, even built the name for jazz. Jazz was never used to music until Brown gave it its advance. The colors are not responsible as the great big ballyhoo. It was done by the north, the kid the south. The colors only play plantation and jazz is the part of swing. You can see how well it has done as they're all having fun telling what they've done to create jazz. It was started in 1915. Don't be fooled. It wasn't until then. Everyone has taken copy and claiming that he's the one. The world is misunderstood. The great point of jazz. There's always room for correction for things done in the past. This is the only way I have to get back at them for something wrongfully done. It's too late to derive any benefits. Let's put it all in song. Give right where right belongs. I just want my public to know the truth. P.S. Tom Brown took the first band to Chicago. You can see how well it has done. This script was composed and written June 3, 1955 by Tom Brown and autographed by all good friends. The signatures. The script. Dominic Alamo. Edward Chance. Pete Palmer. And Arnold J. Loicano. The postscript. Reads. The ray did a lot to perfect this jazz. Gus variated to the strainer's swing. Arnold played the golf air piano. While Bill added tempo to the strain. Tom played a kind of lick here and there. To add to this beautiful tone. Tom, when they're all together, you had the finest jazz in the land.
